summary: @servicetitan/titan-chatbot-ui preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute a 727KB obfuscated payload
details: The package declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. `setup.mjs` is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex-suffix identifiers such as `_0x488df8`/`_0x52943e`/`_0x548d91`, per-function proxy maps like `{YCZJE, QkQej, JBhWy}` mapping opaque keys to string constants and wrapped calls) and, on install, downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...`, extracts it to a temporary directory, `chmod 0o755`s it, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'])`. If a local `bun` binary already exists, the same sibling `math_init.js` is executed directly. `math_init.js` is a 727,680-byte single-line `@bun @bun-cjs` module with a large mixed numeric/string constant array, an array-rotation decoder (`WV8StW`), and a string-array lookup routine (`hc1jfK9`) — a javascript-obfuscator string-array + control-flow-indirection layout. The package is advertised as a React chatbot UI component library; rendering React components does not require pulling in an alternate language runtime at install time or executing an obfuscated 727KB blob. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern deliberately routes payload execution through Bun so that standard Node.js-oriented review of the package does not evaluate what actually runs on installer machines.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
